I pride myself on living a busy life, but that means I have to work really hard to reduce cognitive load. I love having a clean home, but between running to events and keeping up with work, it’s hard to remember to. I didn’t think a robot vacuum was the solution until I read my colleague’s review of the Roborock Saros 10R. Seeing the way it took care of her hardwood floors, I was convinced to give the vacuum brand a try. I decided to test Roborock’s newest model of 2026: the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Industry observers note that though the Saros 10R has some powerful suction of its own, I chose the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro for two reasons: its ability to lower into tight spaces, and its more powerful mopping speed. After over two months of testing, I’m thrilled with how much time I’ve saved. This is like having a cleaning service come through before I host; someone’s at home vacuuming while I’m out picking up dinner party ingredients.

Best for: Cluttered family homes or a single person’s apartment.

Not ideal for: A budget-friendly first vacuum purchase or a home with lots of stairs.

Price at review: $849.99, discounted from $1,499.99.

Recent findings suggest that bottom Line: This robot vacuum and mop is absolutely worth the premium for the time and headache saved. It’s great for homes with lots of different floor types, from hardwood and tile to scattered rugs of different piles.

Recent findings suggest that half of the genius of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is in the dock, so it does take up some floor real estate. The vacuum itself is just over 13 inches wide and three inches tall, and the camera mounted on top retracts for low-clearance access under furniture or cabinets. The dock itself measures 17.72 in × 15.83 in x 19.45 in, so be sure you’ll have that amount of space for it to live, plus room for the vacuum to exit and park itself.

In a recent development, the dock holds the mop pads, clean and dirty water tanks, and the dustbin that the robot vacuum empties into. On the underside of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3, there are dual spinning pads for mopping, and they can extend to get to your most annoying edges and corners. There’s also a sweeping tool and tangle-resistant brush to vacuum. A sweeping arm reaches out to stir up any dirt and debris before powerful suction takes care of it.

Recent findings suggest that the camera on top is what makes it a smart vacuum. It scans and learns your home with AI detection that’s pretty spot-on, but you can make adjustments as needed. You can have it clean custom zones or specific rooms, so if there’s just one spill in the kitchen, it won’t head for the bathroom.

Is it too cliché to say it works like a dream? I didn’t know how badly I needed this vacuum until I had it. Its vacuum function is ideal for regular maintenance and surface-level cleans, and so helpful for last-minute tidying before the guests come. And the mopping feature is super smart, especially for homes like mine that vary between rugs, hardwood, and tile. The Qrevo Edge 3 Pro vacuums the carpeted areas first so your rugs don’t get wet. And if it needs to travel over rugs to get to hardwood, it’ll actually lift the mop pads up or physically detach and leave the pads behind.

Industry observers note that when you first set it up, it’ll travel your home, making a digital map of the floor material, surface area, furniture, and any potential obstacles, like a power strip with long wires. You really need to clear the floor beforehand to let it do its best work.

Industry observers note that sadly, the map isn’t easy to adjust, so if you’re someone constantly rearranging your furniture, you will also be resetting the map. But if you’re like me and stick to one layout once it’s set, it knows your home like the back of your hand. And then it works quickly and accurately. Remember to leave closet doors closed or open, depending on what you want it to clean. This makes it easy to adjust if you don’t want it to wander into a closet—it won’t push open a door.

Industry observers note that as it travels my apartment floor, it reliably dodges charging cables, shoelaces, socks, and any other trip hazards. If anything, it’s a little too cautious, but once it finishes a pass, you can see in the app what the vacuum considered an obstacle, and correct it if need be.

In a recent development, I love being able to see the exact path it took, so I know if there are any corners it missed. I set a few shortcut cleaning modes with set routines, like Bathroom Deep Clean when I want it to scrub the floors of my walk-in shower with extra strength. The “Happy Working Song” routine triggers a deep clean of the whole place.

Recent findings suggest that this is a robot vacuum that lives up to its hefty price tag. It’s the kind of automation I used to picture watching The Jetsons. For one thing, it’s voice-activated. I named mine Giselle after the movie Enchanted, but all models activate when you say “Hello, Rocky.” I can give it a command like “clean the bathroom,” and it’ll set off on its way. And once it’s done with its cleaning routine, it takes care of every bit of maintenance. It self-empties into a spacious, sealed dustbin. It drains dirty water, washes the mop pads in boiling water, and dries them with heated air. So there are no soggy bacterial centers for me to deal with. All I have to do is empty the dirty water down the drain.

It has been revealed that there’s a remote control option too. You can either look through the camera of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro to see where it’s going, or control it like an RC car toy. This is why it’s my best tool for hosting—I can run out and grab the groceries while tracking where it’s headed. And with the included microphone, I can “call” Giselle and my voice will speak through the vacuum cleaner. I could speak to someone while away from home or check on a pet. It’s like a nanny cam on wheels. It also comes with its own light for cleaning dim areas, but I find it does its best work in daylight.

According to recent reports, A robot vacuum is only worth its salt if it’s more helpful than it is tedious to maintain. I’m happy to say that’s the case with Giselle. After mopping, there’s no excessive water left behind. It dries super quickly. And it takes not even 10 seconds to empty the dustbin, mess-free. Washing the mop takes five minutes; however, drying the mop takes two to three hours.

Recent findings suggest that A few notes on cleaning: you will want to empty the dirty water tank every time you run the mop. Because the tank is out of view, it can get gross in there if you forget to wash it out. I learned that the hard way. That’s the only step the Roborock doesn’t do for you. But light scrubbing with some Dawn is all it needs. You don’t need to change the dust bag often (I haven’t needed to in over a month of testing).

Industry observers note that I have to provide a few disclaimers on my use of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro. I live alone, so I can’t speak to how it interacts with kids or other adults in the home. I tend to just stay on the couch and out of Giselle’s way while the vacuum is running. I have short hair and no pets, so I can’t really speak to tangle resistance, either. I also live in a single-floor home, so it’s important to note that if you have multiple floors, you still have to manually carry the robot up or down the stairs. However, the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro supports Multi-Level Mapping, so it’ll memorize and recognize which floor it’s on and start the cleaning cycle in seconds. No need to recalibrate.

In a recent development, as far as volume goes: when I’m in the same room, I find it too loud for a phone call without some kind of noise cancellation. But when it’s in a different room, I forget it’s running. The loudest feature is when it’s emptying into the dock, which is a small price to pay for automation.

Roborock’s newest robo-vacuum and mop is definitely one of the more premium options on the market, but it’s worth the investment. The smart obstacle avoidance and self-maintenance features take away the stress of cleaning.

Sources indicate that the Roborock Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is such a huge help for anyone who wants a cleaner home but doesn’t have the time to put in the elbow grease to clean every room. I’m so much calmer knowing my home is being cleaned while I work or multitask. It knows my home so well, even with so many different floor materials to navigate. I love this so much that I’d run this while I sleep (if I didn’t think it’d bother my neighbors). And with the current Black Friday deal running on Amazon, it’s nearly half off, so now is the best time to get one!

They’re also quite durable and are naturally water-repellant, and the cashmere lining adds warmth on the inside.

It has been revealed that commerce Editor Luke Guillory loves these merino wool-lined deerskin gloves from Geier Gloves, a brand that has been making leather products in the U.S. for almost a century. Since the brand specializes in leather, you can bet the deerskin on these gloves is of the highest quality, and the wool lining is very nice, too. Geier also makes a lot of wor, driving, and motorcycle gloves, so you know they’re the real deal. The black and brown colorways look quite polished, but the natural and saddle leather options are also great.

If you want a nice luxurious pair of cashmere gloves, go with these ones from Sunspel. Lately, I’ve been wearing these gloves, which were knitted in Scotland from super soft pure cashmere. The brand has been perfecting the craft for over 150 years, so you can trust that these are the best of the best. It’s basically like enveloping your hands in a cozy blanket. For a full set, get the brand’s cashmere hat and scarf.

Recent findings suggest that these Canada Goose gloves are basically the equivalent of wearing a puffer jacket on your hands. With heavy-duty, long rib-knit cuffs for extra protection and 750-fill-power down on the inside, your hands will stay warm and dry without their mobility being super impacted by something extra bulky. Note that these have a touchscreen-compatible index finger but not thumb.

Wool-blend gloves are as handsome as any of the very best sweaters in your rotation. Even though the outside is made from knit material, the insulated interior will keep your hands warm and dry during your next epic snowball fight. They’re also thin enough to layer under another pair of gloves if it’s really freezing outside.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to gloves, there’s one brand I’ve trusted for years, and that’s Smartwool. Their gloves are warm without being bulky, and mine have lasted for years. Having a warm pair of gloves that actually does its job well is even more important for my boyfriend, who has Raynaud’s and needs extra protection for his hands, and the gloves he relies on year after year? Also Smartwool. These newly introduced fleece gloves from the brand have extra insulation on the back to provide serious warmth, and they’re also functional with touchscreen-compatible pads on the thumbs and index fingers. Sure, they’re a little expensive for fleece gloves at $68—but if you don’t need the extra insulation, you can try the regular Active Fleece Gloves for $48.

Industry observers note that if all you need is a solid pair of knit gloves and you’re not looking to spend a fortune, look no further than Uniqlo. The brand’s Heattech knit gloves are soft and warm and have effective touchscreen-compatible fingertips. They also come in 11 fun colors, so you might as well get a couple pairs for yourself—and they make a great holiday gift for literally anyone.

You already know we love Barbour’s waxed canvas jackets, so it’s no surprise we’re also a fan of the brand’s stylish, preppy gloves. These leather-palmed gloves have a cotton tartan face for a cool contrast and wool lining on the inside for extra warmth—and they’re waterproof, so you can break them out no matter what’s going on with the weather. Pair these with the Barbour Beaufort jacket for an iconic look.

In a recent development, knit gloves are great when it comes to keeping warm, but they’re not the best when it’s raining or snowing. No one wants a pair of soaking gloves (that probably make your hands feel even colder). Enter these waterproof gloves from the brand that brought you the famous Bean Boots. With a waterproof nylon exterior and a down fill, they’ll keep rain and show out while keeping your hands warm. Note that some say the fingers are long, so consider that when choosing a size.

Industry observers note that when you’re stuck in a blizzard or your location is prone to unpredictable weather, you’ll need something a little more heavy duty. REI’s weatherproof gore-tex gloves will give your hands the protection they need. They’re also essentially a two-in-one: The removable fleece liners can be used on their own or with the weatherproof outers as an extra layer of warmth.

In a recent development, naadam’s famous cashmere sweater is one of our favorite pieces of winter clothing and one of our go-to gifts for the holidays, birthdays, Valentine’s Day, etc. The brand makes a matching pair of soft cashmere gloves, which come in 13 colors and are under $100. A genius gift idea? Get them the sweater with a matching pair of gloves, and they’ll wear both all winter long.

If you want that classic Sherlock Holmes leather glove look, you have lots of choices. But if you don’t want to spend a ton on a pair, get these $60 gloves from Quince. Not only do they have a nice leather exterior in either brown or black, they also have a cashmere lining on the inside.

In a recent development, on the high end of the high end, Gucci has a gorgeous luxury pair of leather gloves with the brand’s signature horsebit on the wrist for a fun little detail. Made from leather and silk, these are soft, smooth, and very stylish.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour may have wrapped in September, but fans will soon get another chance to experience it. Following an initial teaser on November 23, the singer declared on November 24 that both a concert film and a documentary for the tour are set to premiere on Peacock.

The news comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.

Here’s everything we know about the projects so far.

The documentary—titled The Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour —follows Grande “during the 30 days leading up to the opening of her sold-out tour as she and her team race to bring the ambitious production to life,” according to Peacock. “At the same time, Grande is putting the finishing touches on her eighth studio album, giving audiences an intimate window into her creative process during a pivotal moment.”.

The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film “journeys through the collapse of her reality, a cosmic rebirth, a reconnection with her inner child, and the memories that shaped her. She transforms the Eternal Sunshine Tour into a cinematic celebration of healing, connection, and the music that has defined her life.”.

In a recent development, her Eternal Sunshine Tour began in Oakland, California, on June 6 and concluded on September 1 following 10 performances at London’s O2 Arena. The reveals featured music from across her discography, including Eternal Sunshine, Positions, and her latest album, Petal, which was released in July.

Industry observers note that the tour also marked Grande’s return to the concert stage following her 2019 Sweetener World Tour. Throughout the run, she performed in custom looks from designers including Alexander McQueen, Givenchy, and Vivienne Westwood, styled by Law Roach.

Grande shared the first teaser on Instagram on November 23, in collaboration with Peacock and Team Ariana.

The video features footage of Grande performing the title track from Eternal Sunshine. As the performance ends, the screen reveals the message: “Coming soon to… Peacock.”.

During an August interview with Vosk in the City, Grande reflected on how her latest tour differed from her previous experiences performing live.

“I think my last tour I wasn’t necessarily in the same place in life, and I wasn’t able to be as present as I am this time,” she explained, describing the Eternal Sunshine Tour as “such a beautiful corrective experience.”.

Grande also spoke about reconnecting with longtime fans through songs spanning more than a decade of her career.

It has been revealed that in August, her representative confirmed that the singer planned to step away from public-facing work following the tour. Grande later addressed the decision during a concert in Chicago, explaining that it had been made well in advance.

“It is something that I have decided; it’s a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago, and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the audience.

It has been revealed that the Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour documentary premieres on Peacock on December 11. The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film arrives on December 12.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
  • Sources indicate that local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
  • Anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

Sources indicate that local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

Anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

It has been revealed that anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

Industry observers note that while you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

In a recent development, anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

Over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber company owner James Everett.

In 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their new “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

Today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their latest primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

Recent findings suggest that pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

According to recent reports, additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even mentioned to be haunted by its own ghost.

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

Is It Rude to Ask Guests to Bring Food for Thanksgiving Dinner?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At its best, Thanksgiving is an opportunity to gather around and share our appreciation for one another through contribution and collaboration.
  • However, there is a right way and a wrong way to broach the issue, and luckily, it’s a topic that the best hosts and advice columnists have adeptly tackled time and time again.
  • In a recent development, the Post Institute’s advice also highlights something important: The onus is very much on the guest to offer to contribute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At its best, Thanksgiving is an opportunity to gather around and share our appreciation for one another through contribution and collaboration. But let’s be honest, any holiday can be a minefield, and there’s always something new to navigate—even beyond a dry turkey. One particular concern is preparing a meal that will suit everyone and one large enough to make sure no one leaves hungry. And so, a host may be inclined to ask guests to contribute to the buffet.

However, there is a right way and a wrong way to broach the issue, and luckily, it’s a topic that the best hosts and advice columnists have adeptly tackled time and time again. This begins, perhaps, with the most vaunted of all: Emily Post. Well, her descendants, anyway. The Post Institute suggests that it is acceptable, given the “potluck” nature of the day, to ask guests to contribute, but hosts must “Have a flexible menu strategy...be prepared to be ‘coordination central.’”.

In a recent development, the Post Institute’s advice also highlights something important: The onus is very much on the guest to offer to contribute. Here’s how they should do it: “Offer to contribute to the meal—but don't dictate the menu. Your best bet is to make your offer open-ended and follow your host's direction.” Plus, it never hurts to take responsibility for your own dietary needs, though good hosts will always do their best to accommodate.

Martha Stewart and Ina Garten share similar protocol. In an interview with the Los Angeles Times, Stewart suggests that during potlucks more broadly, “The host can provide the main course,” and the guests can bring the sides. Using her “duck breast with fig sauce menu” (a multi-course dinner party plan starring the namesake dish) as an example, she notes, “One person can bring the braised red cabbage and someone else can prepare the potato pancake or the hazelnut brittle for the ice cream.”.

Garten is enthusiastic about guest contributions, telling Bon Appétit, “I actually love to ask people for help.” She also offers specific marching orders: “I might put somebody in charge of wine if they like wine.” Using a guest’s talents and interests to get to the best outcome is a smart idea, and can even go beyond sweet potatoes and pumpkin pie to napkins or place cards.

Myka Meier, the Beaumont etiquette founder, has an entire treatise on the topic, “A guest who accepts a dinner invitation should not discover the day before that they are responsible for the main course.” Instead, she suggests offering a choice, telling guests: “We are having a potluck supper on Saturday at six. I will make the main dish. Would you enjoy bringing a vegetable side, bread, or dessert?” She also reminds hosts to tell their guests how many are joining.

In a recent development, the most important aspect, as with all facets of Thanksgiving, is to have fun and celebrate with loved ones—be lenient, forgiving, and courteous. With a bit of preparation, everything will turn out well.

Dorothy Scarborough (she/her) is the assistant to the Editor in Chief of Town & Country and Elle Decor.

Fascia Release Is the Key to Regulating Your Nervous System, Getting Better Sleep, and Improving Skin

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders.
  • Sources indicate that “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions.
  • In a recent development, once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders. Within minutes, tears prick my eyes. I’m familiar with the sudden catharsis bodywork can bring, but this is different. Known as “myofascial release”—a targeted therapy that works with fascia, the continuous matrix of connective tissue that wraps every muscle, nerve, and organ—it aims to reduce tightness and release restricted tissue, restoring its natural glide.

Sources indicate that “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions. “When you move or hold stress, forces are transmitted through this interconnected system. It senses everything and dictates how the whole body responds. This treatment directly influences how we perceive and react to tension.”.

In a recent development, once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web. “It’s part of a complex system involving movement, circulation, lymphatics, posture, and tissue health,” Alibhai explains. When it works well, it keeps everything moving and prevents systems from becoming sluggish, but when it becomes restricted, often from scrolling, sedentary habits, or chronic stress, the fluid between the layers can thicken. This affects physical mobility and emotional well-being, leading to issues ranging from pain and stiffness to a dysregulated nervous system.

Fascia and neurology are intrinsically linked, explains skin-health expert Annee de Mamiel. “Fascia changes according to how we move, breathe, and repeatedly load the body,” she notes. “Cortisol and adrenaline change our physiology; the nervous system alters breathing, muscular tone, and stress response. Over time, these repeated patterns affect the tissues.” It’s a catch-22: greater stress can tighten fascia, which in turn can send your body into fight-or-flight mode, prolonging the anxiety that caused the damage in the first place.

This mind-body connection is just one reason why fascia has piqued the wellness industry’s interest. Google searches for “fascia release” have soared in the past year, while facials targeting the system are becoming more popular. Robert Schleip, the director of the Fascia Research Group at Ulm University, attributes this to its holistic possibilities. “Fascia is now studied in relation to the autonomic nervous system, and therefore emotional regulation, as well as the immune system and aging,” he says. The latest findings show that supporting your fascia goes far beyond easing a tight neck; it's linked to reduced arterial stiffness and improved cardiovascular health.

Fascia release has also entered the skin-health conversation. Tight fascia can be an overlooked culprit behind loss of luminosity, puffiness, and premature aging, says de Mamiel, because it’s heavily involved in fluid drainage and lymphatic pathways. “The diaphragm plays a role in pressure changes and fluid movement through the body, and the fascial system connects these areas,” she explains. “When I work on movement and tension through the neck, chest, and rib cage, I often see a change in how congested or puffy the face appears.” However, releasing fascia effectively doesn't require aggressive force. “If I use so much pressure that your body braces, I’ve produced the opposite response—it’s about creating conditions where the nervous system and tissue can both settle.”.

Recent findings suggest that facialist Nichola Joss achieves similarly impressive results with her signature Inner Facial, which fuses lymphatic drainage, fascia release, buccal massage, and sculpting techniques. “Fascia surrounds and supports our muscles; when restricted, it affects how freely muscles move,” Joss explains. This affects lymphatic flow and your skin’s natural glow. “By releasing muscular and fascial tension, you lift, tone, and sculpt contours while boosting circulation and softening fine lines.”.

Recent findings suggest that beyond professional treatments, supporting fascial health depends on consistent daily habits. First, fascia thrives on varied movement: try walking, twisting your body, reaching overhead, and squatting to support overall health. Unfortunately, there are no true quick fixes: Spending the day glued to an office chair and then going straight into an intense HIIT session can actually be counterproductive. Instead, interrupt patterns throughout the day: Stand during phone calls instead of sitting, swing your arms gently during screen breaks, and make sure you’re not holding your breath during stressful periods at work. Counteract hours spent hunched over a device with this simple doorway stretch: Place your forearms against the frame, step forward gently, and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply.

Recent findings suggest that schleip recommends aligning exercise with your circadian rhythm. “Incorporate dynamic, elastic, or bouncing movements in the morning, ideally outdoors, and slow stretches in the evening,” he suggests, adding that sustained yoga positions, such as a child’s pose held for at least 30 seconds, can be particularly helpful. “Regular stretching improves joint mobility and may benefit cardiovascular markers such as arterial stiffness,” he adds. Finally, make nutrition and hydration a priority: fascia is 70 percent water and needs hydration to glide freely.

As Alibhai reflects at the end of my session: “The goal isn’t to constantly release fascia; it’s to keep your body moving, adaptable, and well nourished.” I leave feeling lighter and more grounded—and I instinctively skip the Tube and walk home.

According to Whitney Ray, owner of Wyeth Ray Interiors, one reason that hosting Thanksgiving feels so special is that it's the one time of year most hosts actually break out their nice tableware. However, she believes you should be using these beautiful and sentimental pieces more often.

Sources indicate that "So many people wait to use their best serving and dinnerware pieces at holidays like Thanksgiving, but I say those beautiful dishes should be used all year long," she states. Hovik Harutyunyan is an event designer, etiquette specialist, and the founder of Harutyunyan Events. He believes that one key logistical trick a host can apply to any dinner or party they host is curating a menu full of familiar foods that are easy to prepare ahead.

"Thanksgiving menus work so well because the recipes are familiar as well as tried-and-true," he notes. "For example, let's talk about the pies. Thanksgiving dessert is so easy because most of us opt for pumpkin and pecan pie. We know the dessert, and it's extremely easy to make in advance.".

In a recent development, he also notes that it's best not to try out complicated, brand-new recipes for a major hosting event. You should opt for an elevated menu that is easy to scale and distribute across a large number of guests.

Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving is one meal where guests love contributing by bringing a side dish or dessert. While not every gathering needs to have a potluck element, there are other ways you can lighten your cooking load.

It has been revealed that christina Samatas and Renee DiSanto are principals of Park & Oak, and DiSanto is also the owner of Marcel’s Culinary Experience, a culinary community and cooking school. Both of them fully endorse taking a few shortcuts when it comes to hosting any major dinner.

In a recent development, "Not every detail needs to be homemade to feel special," DiSanto indicates. "There are many ways to save you a few steps, such as using pre-cut veggies or incorporating a few prepared appetizers or sides. Spend more time on the details that matter the most to you, rather than the little things.".

According to recent reports, for any event you hold, it's pretty much inevitable that guests always end up in the kitchen. "Whether you invite guests in or not, Thanksgiving demonstrates us the kitchen is where people naturally congregate before a meal, whether they are wanting to help or simply catch up before dinner is served," Ray indicates.

Industry observers note that for this reason, she notes you should always plan to entertain in the kitchen at any gathering. Consider adding small bites and a drinks station on your kitchen counter or island, and try to clean as you go while making the meal.

Sources indicate that thanksgiving is a celebration of gratitude, and Harutyunyan believes you should apply the same spirit to any party. Anytime you gather with loved ones is an opportunity to give them a special experience.

"Thanksgiving, and the holidays in general, is one of the most magical times of the year," he notes. "As stressful and chaotic as they may be, we love to gather with our loved ones to enjoy each other's company. We share stories, memories, and gratitude. In a recent development, most memory foam mattresses start to cave in, turn yellow, sag, pill, or fray, but not the Nectar. It becomes more comfortable and molds to your body over time. The Classic bed has six layers, each of which provides a different perk, from cooling to support to motion isolation. We have a queen-size mattress at home, and I can hardly feel my husband get up or move around in bed. Plus, changing the fitted sheet is a breeze because the mattress isn’t heavy to lift.

I have tested mattresses that cost thousands of dollars and slept on countless beds at five-star hotels, yet I keep coming back to the Nectar as my ultimate favorite. The queen is only $699 right now during Black Friday/Cyber Monday, which is an insane steal. Typically, it’s $1,567, which still isn’t a terrible price considering most luxury mattresses will cost over $3k.

Recent findings suggest that over the years, we’ve managed to convince a few people to get this mattress, too, especially if they spend a night or two on it. After my husband’s cousins crashed on our Nectar Classic mattress once, they immediately asked what brand it was and bought one for their home, too.

Funnily enough, my sister-in-law and her husband were also complaining about the mattress in their guest room, and now I’m thinking...should I just replace theirs too with a Nectar? I’m sure my in-laws won’t mind, right?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if Eloise had the Plaza, Valentina De Santis had the Grand Hotel Tremezzo, the luxury Lake Como resort her family has owned and operated for three generations.
  • In 2016, De Santis took over as CEO and, by 2022, she and her parents had bought a nearby 18th-century villa and transformed it into another five-star hotel, Villa Passalacqua.
  • In our On the Couch survey, we asked De Santis about all the places, people, and pieces that inspire her.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if Eloise had the Plaza, Valentina De Santis had the Grand Hotel Tremezzo, the luxury Lake Como resort her family has owned and operated for three generations. A Como native who spent her early career consulting at Bain & Company, she began working at the property in an official capacity in 2010, the year of its centenary. “Unofficially,” she tells us, “I clocked in as a child, running through the corridors and convinced the whole hotel depended on me.”.

In 2016, De Santis took over as CEO and, by 2022, she and her parents had bought a nearby 18th-century villa and transformed it into another five-star hotel, Villa Passalacqua. As De Santis’s portfolio continues to expand, she finds comfort in working with her family and the team that’s known her for her whole life: “People who grow with you, believe in what you are building, and care about it as much as you do, that’s everything.”.

In our On the Couch survey, we asked De Santis about all the places, people, and pieces that inspire her. She also divulges a few of her best travel recommendations—both in Como and beyond.

In a recent development, describe your studio in three words: Full. Of. Chaos.

Greatest Influences: My parents, my first and forever creative directors.

Favorite Eras of Design: The Belle Époque, when more was more and every room seemed to have a little champagne in its veins.

Industry observers note that favorite Sofa: A Daisy curved Italian midcentury sofa from the 1950s. It's beautifully sculptural, it's pink. It's Gio Ponti.

Sources indicate that maverick design style trick: Break one rule. If everything in a room is behaving, something is missing.

Recent findings suggest that most beloved buildings: Villa Necchi Campiglio in Milan. When I lived in the city, it was right on my doorstep, so I was there all the time. And always, always a little hello to the pink flamingos next door!

Architect you admire: Not the substantial name you’d expect, but the one closest to my heart, Ico Parisi. He made a real difference in my family’s story. He taught my parents how to look at art, and how to love it, and I grew up seeing the world through that same eye.

Destination Museum: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice and the Fondation Maeght in Saint-Paul-de-Vence. Before they were museums, they were the homes of great collectors, and it reveals. You half expect the host to walk in and offer you a drink. With Casabianca, we hope to bring the same magic to my parents’ collection. Peggy, I hope you approve.

According to recent reports, go-to galleries: Lia Rumma in Milan. It has a strong point of view and never plays it safe. It is where we found one of Anselm Kiefer’s Women of Antiquity, which now lives at Casabianca. I’ll never forget my mother’s face the day we saw her; that was when we knew she was coming home with us.

Favorite Artist: Mark Rothko. My wildest dream is to have one in my living room, one of those enormous canvases where color doesn’t just sit on the surface; it explodes, then slowly pulls you in.

Vintage Piece of Your Dreams: An original Margherita by Franco Albini for Bonacina. Yes, I know, more from the ’50s! I clearly have a type. I love how sculptural it is, while the woven rattan keeps it feeling warm and relaxed.

According to recent reports, favorite getaway: Puglia. I have spent so many summers there with my family that it feels like a second home.

It has been revealed that hotels to Check Into: The Amalfi Coast is hard to beat. In my opinion, some of the best hotels in the world are concentrated in just a few miles, each one an incredible house. On top of that, they are all dear friends, so I would love to check into every one of them. But my favorite memory? Lemon linguine on the terrace of the Santa Caterina.

Best Shop for Gifts: Chez Dédé in Rome. Daria and Andrea are dear friends, and the co-authors of our Passalacqua book, and everything in their shop seems to come with a story. My favorite is their Lettera d’Amore necklace, a love letter you can actually wear.

Industry observers note that best Host/Hostess Gift: Something made with your own hands, or close enough! Olive oil from your grove, homemade biscuits, chocolate-dipped orange peel. Add a handwritten note, and it beats anything you could ever buy.

Industry observers note that entertaining Tips: Always have more food than you need. Italian mothers have taught me this much.

Style Icons: Lady Di. I’ve had a crush on her since I was a little girl, and honestly, I never got over it.

Industry observers note that fashion Designers: JJ Martin (La DoubleJ) for the extraordinary way JJ brings color, print, and joy into fashion. Emilia Wickstead for her beautiful, feminine silhouettes.

Style Tip: Go tone-on-tone. My friend Patrizia, who designs Moresi's collections, taught me there's nothing chicer than a head-to-toe single-color look.

According to recent reports, required Reading: Va' dove ti porta il cuore by Susanna Tamaro. It is the book I have turned to whenever I have had a substantial decision to make, and somehow it always brings me back to the same place: follow your heart.

Cocktail of Choice: A Bellini. It is hard to improve on a classic.

Industry observers note that favorite Restaurant: La Tirlindana on the lake for old-world magic. In Milan, I stay loyal to the classics: Da Giacomo and Savini never miss.

Must-Have Accessory: A great pair of unscratchable sunglasses. I live by a lake, so they are both a fashion accessory and a survival tool.

Watch to Wear: A Cartier Tank Louis Cartier in yellow gold. It has been chic for so long that it has nothing left to prove.

Favorite Jeweler: Felice Gabaglio in Como. I have known Marina and her family for as long as I can remember. My father used to take me there to choose jewelry for my mother, and I was always so excited to discover those little treasures with him. It is still where I go when I want something truly special. And now Marina’s daughters have introduced JAM, a newly introduced contemporary line of their own. So now I have another very good reason to stop by.

Annie Goldsmith is the senior editor and digital lead at ELLE Decor, where she covers design, culture, style, and trends. She previously held positions at The Information, covering technology and culture, and Town & Country, writing about news, entertainment, and fashion. Her work has also appeared in Vogue, Rolling Stone, and the SF Standard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Body is Netflix’s latest buzzy teen psychodrama, and it’s not surprising why. The show, a cross between The Craft, Jennifer’s Body, and Cruel Intentions, follows a group of Catholic high school cheerleaders who sacrifice a newcomer in a pact with Satan to secure a spot in regionals. But when their sacrifice works too well, all of the girls on the team—and the town at large—are left with religious hysteria.

The show promptly caught fire on social media following its arrival on November 11, leaving fans praying for a second installment, but will it return? Here’s everything we know about season 2 of The Body.

According to recent reports, the Body has not been renewed for a second season yet by Netflix. The streamer typically waits a few weeks after a show’s premiere before sharing a season renewal announcement.

No cast members have been confirmed for season 2 yet, but fans are hoping that Kristina Bogic, Sara Boustany, Geena Meszaros, Nnamdi Asomugha, Louisa Krause, Shirley Chen, Jackson Kelly, Sofia Wylie, Kyra Pierce, Phallon Pierce, Marcel Ruiz, Orlando Norman, and Gabby Windey all return to their roles.

Season 1 ends with a few cliffhangers that leave the window open for a potential season 2. In the final episode, Anya finally confesses to head priest Father Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), and Grace finally wakes up, with her first words being “I’m God.”.

Some fans have interpreted Anya’s confession as being the reason why Grace finally wakes up. Gammell didn’t confirm the theory, but she told Deadline, “That’s a fire take...that is Maddie’s prophecy, and if there’s a season 2 we’ll be all over that.”.

Elsewhere in Gammell’s Deadline interview, she opened up about Tyler and Lisbeth potentially sleeping together, which could possibly become its own season 2 plot. “I think if they sleep together, it’s like another great mystery of the show. None of us were there, so none of us really know what happened in that room,” she added. “But I do think Geena has a joke that Lisbeth’s first kiss was the mouth-to-mouth with Grace when she was trying to resuscitate her. So, I don’t know how fast she’s going. She’s just a baby.”.

In an interview with Swooon, Gammell noted that the ending of The Body was “a tease and a setup of everywhere that we wish to go next season, if we’re so lucky to get one.”.

Some of the cast members already have ideas on what they’d like to see happen should The Body receive a season 2 renewal. “We love to pitch stuff to Quinn [Shephard] and Gina [Gammell], like probably too much. They’re so receptive,” Boustany told Swooon, while Bogic added, “We’re all so close, and that was also the tone on set. It was very welcomed [to pitch ideas].”.

The Body season 2 has no release date yet, so fans will have to stay tuned for updates.

It’s time to push your relationships outside of their comfort zone, Gemini! The month starts out with the Sun moving through Sagittarius, highlighting your closest ties. The next few weeks invite you to invest more time and energy into your one-on-one relationships so you can address problems, discuss the future, deepen connections, or part ways if necessary. This is also a season of collaboration—others are eager to work with you, which can bring more contract and client work into your world.

There’s finally more balance in your daily life when Venus enters Scorpio on December 3. You’re better able to navigate certain obligations in your life that have left your feeling like you’re in the trenches. There is more support available to you and you’re also gaining more recognition for all your hard work and effort. This can show up as a raise, a well-deserved compliment, or finally having the emotional courage and resilience to break a bad habit.

Sources indicate that there are important conversations that need to be had in your closest relationships once Mercury enters Sagittarius on December 6. The next few weeks help you explore relationship dynamics—both how you show up in your closest relationships and also how others show up for you. There may be some issues you need to address, or even helpful conversations that pave the way for the future. This is an exciting time to share ideas and collaborate with others, bringing latest ideas, perspectives, and opportunities your way.

Sources indicate that A Newly introduced Moon in Sagittarius on December 8 brings new relationship milestones your way. This can mark the start of a new relationship or business contract. You might also feel a sense of renewal in existing relationships, helping you to address what’s been left unsaid so you can create a healthier future together. Shared experiences today that push you outside of your comfort zone also bring more shared memories and joy. Try something new and spice up your closest connections.

You’re setting boundaries in your friendships when Saturn stations direct in Aries on December 10. You might need to confront an matter or even cut someone off! The energy can feel isolating today but also help you recognize the people in your life with whom you feel a genuine sense of belonging. This can also help you sign contracts or stay the course and commit to a longterm goal. You’re ready to lock in!

It’s time to go after your dreams when Neptune stations direct in Aries on December 12. This can show up as a surge of creative inspiration that helps you approach a desire in a latest way. You might also stand out more for your creativity, ability to problem solve with your intuition, or your compassionate nature. People are mesmerized by you and eager to support you, so put yourself and your ideas out there!

In a recent development, conversations leave you with you a lot to contemplate when Jupiter stations retrograde in Leo, also on December 12. You could share something big and important with others that brings a sense of relief, healing or celebration. You might learn lucky or hopeful news. You could also learn something that impacts you personally and shifts your perspective in a big way. Be open to other opinions and conversations; words and decisions you make are impactful today.

The Sun enters Capricorn and the Winter Solstice takes place on December 21, asking you to turn inward. It’s time to stick with a proposal to break down some of your own walls. Breaking: 5 Designer-Approved Ways to Make a Small Bathroom Feel Full of Personality

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (685 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When decorating a small bathroom, it's tempting to stick to the tried-and-tested rules.
  • Just because your bathroom is short on square footage doesn't mean it has to be short on personality.
  • Whether you're working with a compact family bathroom, a downstairs WC, or a tiny en suite, here are five ways to give your space a little more character.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When decorating a small bathroom, it's tempting to stick to the tried-and-tested rules. White walls to make the space feel bigger, minimal accessories to avoid clutter, and perhaps a neutral tile or two. But where's the fun in that?

Just because your bathroom is short on square footage doesn't mean it has to be short on personality. In fact, smaller spaces can be the perfect place to experiment with colors, patterns, and decorating ideas you might hesitate to try elsewhere in your home.

Whether you're working with a compact family bathroom, a downstairs WC, or a tiny en suite, here are five ways to give your space a little more character.

White might be the traditional choice for small bathrooms, but it's certainly not the only option.

Bold colors can make a compact space feel intentional and full of personality, whether you opt for a rich, cocooning shade or something brighter and more playful.

Sources indicate that you could paint the entire room for maximum impact, or introduce color through a single wall, vanity unit, or painted woodwork. For a more cohesive look, try picking out a shade from your tiles and repeating it elsewhere in the room.

Make a Statement With Your Tiles.

If there's one room where you can afford to be a little adventurous with tiles, it's the bathroom.

Colorful square tiles, checkerboard patterns, and interesting layouts can all introduce character without taking up valuable floor space.

And you don't necessarily need to tile every wall either. A bold backsplash behind the basin, a tiled shower enclosure, or a contrasting border can make just as much impact.

For a more understated approach, consider using simple tiles in an unexpected color or experimenting with contrasting grout.

Make the Most of Your Windowsills.

When space is limited, every surface counts—and your bathroom windowsill is the perfect place to introduce a little personality without cluttering your countertops. Pictured here, Annie Sloan's bathroom features a sweeping landscape painted right on the bath panel.

It has been revealed that rather than leaving it bare, use it to display a few carefully chosen accessories. A small vase of fresh flowers or a decorative ceramic ornament can make an otherwise functional space feel more considered.

You could even create a little display by grouping objects of different heights and textures, taking inspiration from the way you might style a shelf in your living room.

It has been revealed that just be careful not to overcrowd the space. A few thoughtfully chosen pieces will make much more impact than a windowsill packed with accessories, and you'll still want to leave enough room to open the window for ventilation.

Bring the Outdoors in With Plants.

Houseplants aren't just for living rooms and bedrooms. They can bring a welcome splash of color and life to a bathroom, softening hard surfaces and making even the smallest space feel more inviting.

Bathrooms can be particularly well suited to tropical plants that appreciate humidity, such as ferns, peace lilies, and orchids, provided they receive enough natural light.

Industry observers note that if you're short on floor space, consider hanging a trailing plant from the ceiling or placing one on a wall-mounted shelf. A pothos cascading from a high shelf can look particularly striking against colorful tiles.

Recent findings suggest that and don't forget about the pots themselves. Colorful ceramics and woven planters can be just as decorative as the greenery they hold.

Sometimes, it's the smallest details that make the biggest impact.

Swap plain towels for colorful or patterned designs, introduce a sculptural soap dispenser, or choose a mirror with an interesting frame.

A brightly colored bath mat can bring an otherwise neutral scheme to life, while coordinating toothbrush holders, storage jars, and trays can make everyday essentials feel more considered.

The trick is to choose a few accessories that complement one another, rather than filling every available surface.

And if you're decorating on a budget, this is one of the easiest ways to experiment with a new look without making any permanent changes.

Is It Rude to Ask Guests to Take Their Shoes Off at Your House?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE Decor editor.
  • You’ve asked guests to dress for dinner.
  • Industry observers note that so, is the request rude?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE Decor editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

You’ve asked guests to dress for dinner. Is it fair to ask them to take part of the outfit off at the door? It’s a small holiday-hosting dilemma with reasonable arguments on either side: The host would rather not have wet boots on the good rug; the guest would rather not spend a cocktail party in stocking feet.

Industry observers note that so, is the request rude? Not inherently, according to the etiquette and entertaining experts we asked. But the occasion, the advance notice, and the room you leave for exceptions all matter. Here’s how to handle it before the doorbell rings.

For some households, taking shoes off is simply what you do when you come in, whether you’re stopping by for coffee or staying for Thanksgiving dinner. There’s a practical argument for keeping the rule during the holidays, too. Stacey Gustafson, Bona’s flooring and cleaning expert, points out that grit tracked in on outdoor shoes can scratch hardwood and wear down its finish over time.

But not every shoes-off request is a bid to preserve perfect floors. Removing outdoor footwear is an established cultural custom in Japan, for example, where the genkan, or entrance area, separates outside from in. What one guest considers an unexpected inconvenience may be an entirely ordinary expression of respect in another person’s home.

For David Jubé, founder of food and entertaining platform The Gourmet Host, the request itself is less of a problem than the way it’s delivered. “Asking guests to take their shoes off is not rude. Making them guess is,” he notes. “The rudeness, when it happens, comes from springing the request at the door with no warning, so a guest finds out in front of everyone that they wore mismatched socks or that their boots take five minutes to unlace.”.

“If you’ve invited guests to dress up for an elegant holiday dinner, asking them to remove their shoes upon arrival can undermine the very experience you’ve invited them to enjoy,” says Erika Gessin, founder and creative director of entertaining brand The Fête Edit. “Shoes are often an intentional part of an outfit.”.

Sources indicate that if shoes are coming off regardless, guests should know before they proposal what to wear. For hosts willing to relax their usual rule, etiquette expert Nick Leighton suggests letting the occasion take precedence: “For larger or more formal gatherings, it’s ideal to just let everyone keep their shoes on and treat the cleaning you’ll have to do afterwards as part of the cost of entertaining.”.

Comfort matters as much as appearance. Amber Dawn Schultheis, creator of hosting and recipe site The Host Notes, points out that some guests need the support of their shoes, especially if they’ll be standing for an extended period. Her preferred approach leaves the decision with them: “Shoes are optional. Do what makes you feel good.”.

Industry observers note that if you’re keeping the rule, make it easy to follow. Jubé suggests writing, “We’re a shoes-off house, so bring cozy socks or slippers if you like” on the invitation. At the door, give guests somewhere to sit while they unlace their boots, a rack or tray to put them on, and a basket of clean slippers or grippy socks. If someone needs to keep their shoes on for health, mobility, or safety reasons, let them do so without asking for an explanation.

Sources indicate that and if you’re the guest? Take your cue from the shoes already by the door, not from what you do at home. If it isn’t clear, Gessin recommends asking quietly: “Would you prefer I take my shoes off?”.

Jubé recommends a sturdy mat outside, a washable one inside, and a boot tray for wet footwear. Gessin suggests washable runners in high-traffic areas—the hall between the front door and the dining room is a good place to start. Those small adjustments let you give guests a choice without spending the party keeping tabs on the floor.

Once everyone is inside, resist the urge to monitor every footprint. “Guests remember how a gathering felt, not whether the floor stayed spotless, and a host fretting over every footprint makes everyone tense,” Jubé indicates.

“Floors can be cleaned tomorrow,” Gessin notes. “How you made your guests feel is what they’ll remember.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon. Not unlike Truman Capote and his "swans," Rich welcomed friends such as Kate Moss, Selma Blair, Sofia Coppola, Maya Rudolph, Natasha Lyonne, Parker Posey, and Winona Ryder to his basement office in the brand’s downtown flagship store, documenting fittings and gab sessions with a Polaroid camera. Now, 163 Mercer, a upcoming book from IDEA named for the store’s address, shares stories and photographs of fashion’s golden years just before digital changed everything.

In a recent development, rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the name “Winona.” "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom. It sold out on day one, and a second printing followed the next year. The experience left him wanting more creative outlets.

163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s. She met Rich when Jacobs and Marc Jacobs International president Robert Duffy sent her to the store to pick out a thank-you gift for her professional hospitality at the Mercer Hotel, where Jacobs often stayed.

It has been revealed that the duo, who are so close that they still speak on the phone every day, began brainstorming a project. "I had the photos of all the other girls, so I knew I wanted to do a book with those pictures," Rich said. They considered wallpaper based on the wall collage or a podcast featuring a different one of the girls per episode, but Cassavetes's film background, including her 2007 directorial debut Broken English, made her the perfect book creative partner. IDEA said yes again.

According to recent reports, they worked at Cassavetes’s Los Angeles apartment, laying out images on her oversized office table. "It's a lot like writing a script, which is why I say I ‘directed’ the book; putting together the layout was like making a movie," she remarked. Rich occasionally asked her to add an edited image, and she agreed. "We have similar tastes, and we were open to each other's opinions. He has a cool eye," she added.

In a recent development, their bond developed when Cassavetes worked down the street. "My title at the Mercer was director of sales, but I was really a VIP manager. I had a basement office, too," she recalled. Before New York's indoor smoking ban in 2003, the two took cigarette breaks indoors. "The logistics helped our friendship, hanging out in each other's offices smoking and having tea.".

The book features images of regular visitors plus some who came once or twice, and the women graciously cataloged their memories for it. Don't expect captions throughout; it reads in parts like an IYKYK story asking viewers to figure out who is in the photo. "We didn't caption every Polaroid; they weren't like social media posts," Rich explained.

Recent findings suggest that nostalgia for an era before our feeds made the post-Covid years the perfect time for Rich to revisit his mementos. The book should appeal to members of Gen Z who are wondering what they missed before social media, and those in Gen X who are longing for a time that felt authentic, rather than conceived in a marketing strategy.

Industry observers note that instead of a feed, Rich created an office mood board wall that started with tear sheets and magazine covers of the girls in Marc Jacobs, then added fitting-room Polaroids, which grew more playful, plus newspaper clippings and memorabilia. He likened it to his childhood bedroom, which was covered in Charlie's Angels photos. Cassavetes says the mood board’s special quality was its esoteric nature. "The wall wasn't for a million people to admire. We had privacy. We had fun because we had more freedom.".

Sources indicate that trust bound everyone involved. Rich knew Moss previously, and Cassavetes knew Sofia and Ryder; Rich met the others on the job. Ryder came into the shop independently, and Rich professed his love of Girl, Interrupted. “’That's a girl's movie,’ she noted, and I said, ‘I'm a girl's movie guy,’” Rich recalled. Ryder's infamous 2001 shoplifting case led to her starring in the brand's spring 2003 campaign, appearing on its "Protect the Skin You're In" T-shirts and wearing Marc Jacobs to court.

"Selma didn't know the others,” Rich said. “We hit it off when she tried on the Courrèges–inspired collection. I took Polaroids, sent some to Marc, and kept others. She kept coming in. I introduced her to Kate, Missy, and Frankie Rayder, all of them.”.

Recent findings suggest that the mood differed from today's brand-celebrity ecosystem of mutual monetary gain. "It was unpretentious; no one was there to get paid. We were hanging out and having fun. That was the Marc Jacobs spirit: more artsy, less corporate. It was a perfect zeitgeist moment," Cassavetes said.

It has been revealed that case in point: Rich met Hilary Swank before her Oscar win for Boys Don't Cry. "She would come to the store, and I would dress her up for all the pre-Oscar award demonstrates and events. I put her in a tiered ruffle sundress with a beachy vibe for the Independent Spirit Award in 2000," he recalled.

It has been revealed that impromptu gatherings were plentiful. Once, Moss, Ryder, and Patric Reeves ended up in the office together. "I stocked my fridge with Sofia champagne cans. They were small but potent," Rich mentioned with a chuckle. An image in the book documents the mini party. Though Polaroids waned in popularity after the brand declared bankruptcy and digital cameras and camera phones arrived, Rich kept a stockpile he used until 2015.

"Sometimes I wouldn't even recognize Winona because she had a new role, hair color, or style," he said. "But I met all the boyfriends, watched them get married, pregnant, have babies, and divorce.".

Getting It girls to wear Marc Jacobs was simple. "Marc's clothes were unbelievable; you didn't have to beg them," noted Rich, adding that the store's cool yet friendly vibe helped. "I was a major fan of Marc's, and that radiated to everyone I hired," including bartenders, who made great sales associates because "they knew how to talk to people." A generous clothing allowance, four outfits a season instead of uniforms, fueled employee enthusiasm.

According to recent reports, cassavetes remembers Rich's relaxed styling approach. "He made sure the girls didn't wear the same thing." Rich credits his former boss. "Marc liked everybody's take on his clothes. Winona would change the buttons or redo straps; he loved it.".

In a recent development, costume designer June Ambrose's favorite memories include discovering hidden treasures in the basement. "Robert has an incredible eye and instinctively knew what I needed; I could trust him. He understood the woman, the attitude, and the personality behind the clothes," she wrote in an email. "He made me fall in love with Marc Jacobs.".

Rich also gave his editor and stylist friends early access to sample sales.

His Marc Jacobs career began when Joe Zee took him to his first runway show for the brand. "I was blown away and marched backstage and asked Marc for a job," Rich said. In 1999, he became store manager, eventually rising to vice president of public relations for retail stores during his tenure.

Before 163 Mercer became the Marc Jacobs store in 1997, it was once the Tony Shafrazi Gallery, which propelled the careers of Francis Bacon, David LaChapelle, and Keith Haring, for whom Rich once worked. "There was nothing in SoHo; Marc could have picked any space. There was good energy there. Tony would stop in and regret having given the space up," Rich mentioned, noting Jacobs kicked off SoHo’s current designer shopping enclave.

"The store was so laid-back and a fun, creative safe space. It was also the center of the downtown fashion world at that time," Cassavetes added.

Rich hints that a third book would move away from SoHo. "We wouldn't just be in the office. Maybe it would be pictures from everywhere.".

It has been revealed that yes. In September 2026, Variety confirmed that The Beast in Me would return for a second season on Netflix.

It has been revealed that “We always told ourselves we’d only do a second season of The Beast in Me if we found a story that was worthy of the first—and I’m thrilled to say we found it,” Gordon said in a statement. “We loved making this show and our audience seemed to love watching it, so we’re enormously grateful to Jinny Howe and Netflix, and to Karey Burke and 20th Television for giving us the chance to get the band back together and do it again.”.

On November 3, Deadline revealed that Lili Taylor (Outer Range, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping) joined the cast in a series regular role as Fiona, Aggie’s stepmother.

On November 19, Netflix revealed that Riley Keough (Daisy Jones & The Six, Under the Bridge) and Lorelei Olivia Mote (They Know, The Rescue, Daisy Jones & The Six) will join the show as series regulars for season 2, while Aaron Paul (Breaking Bad, Fallout), Taip Ceman (Cupertino, The Families Stone), and Matthew James Thomas (Accused, Summer of Rockets) join as recurring guest stars.

Gordon discussed the ending of season 1 with The Wrap and what it made him consider for season 2.

Industry observers note that “I think that to the extent that Aggie is a writer who has been delivered to this next stage of her life, whatever that stage is,” he shared at the time. “If there is a story, there might be more. I am tempted by the character of her grifter father in some way. We’ll see how the show does and if an idea comes. But I think they’d be open to more.”.

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

From Sabrina Carpenter to Dakota Johnson, curtain bangs were among the most fawned-over hairstyles in the past few years. It’s not surprising; they flatter all face shapes and offer the face-framing effect of a fringe without the harshness (or any awkward growing-out stage) of a full, blunt chop.

Curtain bangs are also versatile at any age, and the cut has recently stepped into the spotlight as one of the most flattering styles for mature lengths. Penélope Cruz’s recent red-carpet appearance makes a convincing case for the look.

According to recent reports, "Curtain bangs are one of the most flattering fringe options for mature hair because they soften the face rather than dominate it," explains hairdresser David Cassidy from Hove's Palette & Bristle. "They frame the cheekbones, draw attention to the eyes, and create movement around the front of the hair, which instantly feels more youthful.".

Unlike a blunt fringe, he adds that curtain bangs blend into the rest of the haircut, creating an elegant, modern look with just the right amount of youthfulness.

Here, he explains how to get the perfect curtain fringe for mature hair this winter, along with key styling pointers.

As with any bangs cut, an expert eye and professional hand are key to achieving a look that suits your face shape.

Industry observers note that "The key with curtain bangs on mature hair is softness and proportion," states Cassidy. "You want them to start no shorter than the cheekbone and taper gently into the length. Anything too short or too heavy can feel aging.".

He also emphasizes texture; a slightly broken-up finish keeps them from looking flat and gives a more relaxed, lived-in effect.

"Before committing to curtain bangs, think about your natural hair texture and growth pattern," he adds. "Cowlicks, partings, and how your hair falls when it air-dries all matter. A good stylist will tailor the fringe to work with your hair, not against it. Curtain bangs are versatile. When done well, they grow out seamlessly and can be worn parted, swept back, or tucked away.".

Before you veer away from your signature everyday style, consider how much extra styling time a new fringe might require.

Recent findings suggest that "Curtain bangs are surprisingly low-maintenance if they’re cut properly," says Cassidy. "A medium round brush or even a large Velcro roller at the front while the hair cools will give that soft sweep away from the face.".

Sources indicate that he recommends styling your curtain bangs with the hair dryer angled side to side rather than straight down. "It creates lift without stiffness and keeps your bangs looking light and flattering.".

It has been revealed that owen Wilson is a spiritual guy—and long has been. That’s why it fits so naturally that he would star in a golf series for Apple TV, Stick, in which his character, Pryce Cahill, is often searching to find his perfect zen. And as Wilson jokes, he’s started calling himself “Johnny Flowstate” on the green as he talks to himself through shots.

“I just believe there’s something more going on that you can tap into,” he tells Esquire editor in chief Michael Sebastian on the latest episode of “What I’ve Learned.” The fifty-five-year-old actor, best known for his roles in The Royal Tenenbaums, Wedding Crashers, and Midnight in Paris, even admits that he found himself reaching into the beyond for advice from his late father, TV executive Robert Wilson, in a moment of pure panic before hosting Saturday Night Live in 2021.

“He was already gone at that point, but the night before I was freaking out like, I don’t know if I can do this. I was so nervous, and I was thinking a lot about my dad,” Wilson says. The two were incredibly close, and he reveals that his father actually worked with him and his brothers, actors Luke Wilson and Andrew Wilson, on several of their films. One of which was Wes Anderson’s Rushmore, in which their father wrote Bill Murray’s now-iconic church address to the students: “Take dead aim on the rich boys.".

So, as Wilson found himself full of doubt and fear the night before hosting SNL, he recalls looking up and “literally asking [his father] for help” before falling asleep. “I woke up, just incredibly calm, and I had this conviction of this joke my dad would say that needed to go in my monologue.”.

In a recent development, what was the joke? “That he was the charter member of the 3970 club,” Wilson says, “which stood for ‘three sons, nine high schools, seven colleges, and zero degrees.’”.

Sources indicate that “That wasn’t something he was proud of,” Wilson continues. “That was his way to cope with disappointment, but you could almost say that that joke was worth us having all those struggles in school because that joke has lived longer than another diploma would have.” You can watch the episode above as well as listen on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Industry observers note that luckily, it all worked out for the Wilson brothers. Next up, Owen is set to appear in season 2 of Stick on Apple TV and the Meet the Parents legacy sequel, Focker-in-Law with Ben Stiller. He also takes a liking to Esquire’s suggestion of a Christmas movie with another one of his longtime collaborators, Wes Anderson, in the episode.

“It’s one of the biggest relationships of my life,” Wilson says of his friendship with the director. “Had I gotten into one of the colleges that I applied to, I would never have met Wes. And there’s something I always say to my boys—the idea that you can’t do it alone. If there’s something going wrong, I know I can always call and he’ll always be there for me.”.

Why Working Out Just Twice a Week Could Save Your Life

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (277 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You don't need to exercise every day to reap health benefits, according to a study published in JAMA Internal Medicine.
  • The study defined weekend warriors as those who clocked 75 minutes/week of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes/week of moderate exercise in just two sessions.
  • In a recent development, "It is very encouraging news that being physically active on just one or two occasions per week is associated with a lower risk of death, even among people who do some activity but don't quite meet recommended exercise levels," the study's senior author, associate professor Emmanuel Stamatakis from the University of Sydney, told ScienceDaily in 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You don't need to exercise every day to reap health benefits, according to a study published in JAMA Internal Medicine. Researchers at the University of Sydney found that those who work out just twice a week—they call them weekend warriors—had a lower chance of dying from cancer, cardiovascular disease, or any other cause than those who were sedentary.

The study defined weekend warriors as those who clocked 75 minutes/week of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes/week of moderate exercise in just two sessions. They analyzed surveys of 63,591 respondents and found that active adults—even if infrequently—had a 30 percent lower mortality risk than those who rarely or never exercised. So just two moderate exercise sessions a week can quite literally save your life.

In a recent development, "It is very encouraging news that being physically active on just one or two occasions per week is associated with a lower risk of death, even among people who do some activity but don't quite meet recommended exercise levels," the study's senior author, associate professor Emmanuel Stamatakis from the University of Sydney, told ScienceDaily in 2017. "However, for optimal health benefits from physical activity, it is always advisable to meet and exceed the physical activity recommendations.".

Industry observers note that so all you need to do is log 1 hour and 15 minutes of intense exercise, or 2.5 hours of moderate activity, sometime during the workweek or weekend to stay healthy. Running, walking, dancing like a fool—it doesn't matter. While it might not whittle your waist rapidly, science now proves that it's better than doing nothing at all.

Editor’s note: This story was originally published in 2017.

#215220. Tech Report: Why The Rings of Power Will Never Be the Same After the Season 3 Finale

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1613 w)
